items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: JoAnn my accompanist knows and we play it on occasion

ctx.x: Yeah. Then on occasion they had a unit, like the California Collegiates, and all we played was the overture and for 45 minutes we did nothing. We went downstairs and played poker or whatever, and we’d come back. And I’ll never forget this. The famous tune that they came out with, and JoAnn my accompanist knows and we play it on occasion, was “The Hour of Parting.” It was written in 1928. “The Hour of Parting.” And the famous conductor at the music hall — now see how my mind skips me now — the famous conductor, he…
broke the show in, Erno Rappe. Yeah. And his son was a pretty good saxophone player. Can I tell you something about his son?
